title: Differential Dataflow
subtitle: How incremental data-parallel computation is built on streams of signed changes
throughline: one edge update — inserted, indexed, joined, looped to a fixed point, and emitted as only what changed

chapters.title: The Update Triple
chapters.blurb: Collections are streams of signed changes; the whole framework starts from one (data, time, diff) triple.

steps.title: The Update Triple
steps.coverSubtitle: A collection is an evolving pile of signed changes
steps.displayNarration: Differential dataflow watches a collection change and reports only what changed. It all begins with one tiny update — a `(data, time, diff)` triple.
steps.spoken: Differential dataflow watches a collection change, and reports only what changed. It all starts with one tiny update.

steps.title: An insert is a triple
steps.displayNarration: An **InputSession** buffers each change as a triple: the data, a logical `time`, and a difference. `insert(element)` is just `update(element, 1)`.
steps.spoken: Picture one edge being added to a graph. An input session buffers it as a triple: the data, a logical time, and a difference of plus one.

steps.title: A collection of changes
steps.displayNarration: These triples stream into a **Collection** — `collection.rs`'s evolving pile of updates, exposed as `inner: Stream<T, C>`.
steps.spoken: These triples stream into a collection, which is nothing more than an evolving pile of such updates over time.

steps.title: Differences that cancel
steps.displayNarration: The diff is any **Semigroup**: it can `plus_equals` and report `is_zero`. Updates to the same record accumulate, and a difference of zero is retired.
steps.spoken: The difference is any type that can add and test for zero, a semigroup. When updates to the same record accumulate to zero, they cancel and are quietly retired.

steps.title: Sealing logical time
steps.displayNarration: `advance_to(time)` moves the session's clock; `flush()` ships the buffer and tells timely those earlier times are now closed.
steps.spoken: Advancing the time, then flushing, seals a batch of updates and tells the system those earlier moments are now closed.

steps.title: A delete is just minus one
steps.displayNarration: Removing the edge later is another triple with `diff = -1` — `remove(element)` is `update(element, -1)`. Inserts and deletes share one path.
steps.spoken: Removing the edge later is just another triple, this time with a difference of minus one. Inserts and deletes are the same machinery.

steps.title: Act only where it moves
steps.displayNarration: Because every change is a *signed* update, the engine works only where the collection actually moves — and does nothing elsewhere.
steps.spoken: Because everything is a signed change, the system can act only where the collection actually moves, and do no work anywhere else.

chapters.title: Operators on Collections
chapters.blurb: map, count, distinct — familiar functional operators, recomputed incrementally on every change.

steps.title: Operators on Collections
steps.coverSubtitle: Functional transforms you already know — map, filter, count, join
steps.displayNarration: Differential programs are written as *functional* transforms over collections, using operators like `map`, `count`, and `distinct`.
steps.spoken: Differential programs are written as functional transforms over collections, using operators you already know.

steps.title: Map rewrites each record
steps.displayNarration: Start with a collection of edges. `map(|(src,_dst)| src)` rewrites each record — here keeping only the source — carrying its difference along.
steps.spoken: Start with a collection of edges. Map rewrites each record, here extracting just the source node, while carrying its difference along untouched.

steps.title: Count groups by key
steps.displayNarration: `count_total()` groups records by key and reports how often each appears, so every source node gets its out-degree.
steps.spoken: Count total groups records by key and reports how many times each appears, so every source gets its out-degree.

steps.title: Map again
steps.displayNarration: A second `map(|(_src, cnt)| cnt)` keeps only the degree value and discards the node identity.
steps.spoken: Map again, this time keeping only the degree value, throwing away the node.

steps.title: The degree distribution
steps.displayNarration: A second `count_total()` tallies the degrees themselves — the out-degree distribution of the whole graph.
steps.spoken: A second count total tallies the degrees themselves, giving the out-degree distribution of the whole graph.

steps.title: Distinct, a close cousin
steps.displayNarration: `distinct` collapses a collection to one copy of each element. Both `CountTotal` and `ThresholdTotal` require a `TotalOrder` time.
steps.spoken: Distinct is a cousin: it collapses a collection to one copy of each element. Both count and distinct require a totally ordered time.

steps.title: A change ripples through
steps.displayNarration: Change a *single* edge and the update flows only through the operators it actually touches; the rest of the pipeline stays put.
steps.spoken: Now change a single edge. The update ripples only through the operators it actually touches; everything else stays put.

steps.title: map · count · map · count
steps.displayNarration: The whole `hello.rs` pipeline: `map`, `count_total`, `map`, `count_total` — recomputed incrementally on every input change.
steps.spoken: That is the whole pipeline: map, count, map, count, recomputed incrementally on every change.

chapters.title: Arrange & Trace
chapters.blurb: The indexing engine: arrange turns a collection into batches and a shared, compacting trace.

steps.title: Arrange & Trace
steps.coverSubtitle: Indexing a collection into a shared, maintained structure
steps.displayNarration: Joins and reductions need their inputs indexed. **Arranging** a collection builds that shared, maintained index — a `Stream` of batches plus a `Trace`.
steps.spoken: Joins and reductions need their inputs indexed. Arranging a collection builds that shared, maintained index.

steps.title: Index by key
steps.displayNarration: `arrange_by_key` receives the stream of `(data, time, diff)` updates and partitions and indexes them by key across workers.
steps.spoken: Arrange by key receives the stream of update triples and indexes them by key.

steps.title: Frontier carves a batch
steps.displayNarration: When the input frontier advances, the operator carves off a **Batch**: exactly the updates whose times fall in the newly closed range.
steps.spoken: Whenever the input frontier advances, it carves off a batch: exactly the updates whose times fall in the newly closed range.

steps.title: Batches become a trace
steps.displayNarration: Batches accumulate into a **Trace** — logically just the growing sequence of all committed updates `(key, val, time, diff)`.
steps.spoken: Batches accumulate into a trace, which is logically just the growing sequence of all committed updates.

steps.title: Merge and compact
steps.displayNarration: A trace is free to *merge* its batches and *coalesce* times it can prove no reader will tell apart — keeping the total small.
steps.spoken: But a trace is free to merge its batches and to coalesce times it can prove no reader will ever tell apart, keeping it compact.

steps.title: A cursor walks it
steps.displayNarration: A **Cursor** navigates the trace, seeking a `Key` and enumerating its `Val`, `Time`, and `Diff` in order.
steps.spoken: A cursor walks the trace, seeking a key and enumerating its values, times, and differences in order.

steps.title: Built once, shared widely
steps.displayNarration: The same trace can be `import`ed and reused by many operators and even other dataflows — so the index is built once, not per consumer.
steps.spoken: Best of all, the same trace can be imported and reused by many operators and even other dataflows, so the index is built once.

steps.title: The engine underneath
steps.displayNarration: Collection in, arranged, batched on each frontier, merged into a compact trace, and shared out — the engine the heavy operators stand on.
steps.spoken: Collection in, arranged, batched, merged into a trace, and shared out: this is the engine the heavy operators stand on.

chapters.title: Join & Reduce
chapters.blurb: The relational heart: match keyed records across arrangements, then regroup and emit clean differences.

steps.title: Join & Reduce
steps.coverSubtitle: Matching and regrouping records over maintained indices
steps.displayNarration: With inputs arranged, the relational heart of differential dataflow can match and regroup records cheaply — `join` and `reduce`.
steps.spoken: With inputs arranged, the relational heart of differential dataflow can match and regroup records cheaply.

steps.title: Match on the key
steps.displayNarration: `join_core` takes two arrangements and matches their values wherever the keys agree, walking both via cursors.
steps.spoken: The core join takes two arrangements and matches their values wherever the keys agree.

steps.title: Differences multiply
steps.displayNarration: Each match yields a pair, *multiplying* the two diffs. Because multiplication distributes over addition, the result stays correct as inputs change.
steps.spoken: For each match it produces a pair, multiplying the two differences. Because multiplication distributes over addition, this stays correct as inputs change.

steps.title: The closure can filter
steps.displayNarration: The join closure can also drop pairs — for example keeping only `item_a > item_b` so each item meets a strictly smaller partner.
steps.spoken: The join closure can also filter, keeping only the pairs you want, like each item paired with a strictly smaller partner.

steps.title: Reduce groups by key
steps.displayNarration: `reduce` groups the results by key and runs your `logic(key, &[(val, diff)], ...)` over each key's list of values.
steps.spoken: Reduce then groups the results by key and runs your logic over each key's list of values.

steps.title: Retract old, add new
steps.displayNarration: When a key's answer changes, `reduce` retracts the prior output and adds the new one, so downstream sees a clean difference.
steps.spoken: When a key's answer changes, reduce retracts the old output and adds the new one, so downstream sees a clean difference.

steps.title: Use case: recommendations
steps.displayNarration: This is how item-based collaborative filtering counts co-occurrences: a self-`join_core` over interactions, then a `count`.
steps.spoken: This is exactly how collaborative filtering counts item co-occurrences: a self-join over interactions, then a count.

steps.title: Joined, paired, reduced
steps.displayNarration: Two arrangements in, joined on the key, paired with multiplied diffs, reduced by key, and out as a maintained result trace.
steps.spoken: Two arrangements in, joined, paired, reduced, and out as a maintained result.

chapters.title: Iterate to Fixpoint
chapters.blurb: iterate circulates differences through a loop until they dissipate — the engine behind incremental graph analytics.

steps.title: Iterate to Fixpoint
steps.coverSubtitle: Run a fragment over and over until the changes run out
steps.displayNarration: Some answers require repetition. `iterate` runs a differential fragment over and over until the differences dissipate.
steps.spoken: Some answers require repetition. Iterate runs a fragment over and over until the changes run out.

steps.title: Roots enter the loop
steps.displayNarration: Reachability begins with `roots.map(|x| (x, 0))` entering an iterative scope as a **Variable**, each root at distance zero.
steps.spoken: Take reachability. The roots enter an iterative scope as a variable, each marked at distance zero.

steps.title: Step one hop
steps.displayNarration: Each round, the current frontier `join_core`s against the arranged `edges` to step one hop further into the graph.
steps.spoken: Every round, the current frontier joins against the arranged edges to step one hop further into the graph.

steps.title: Keep the minimum
steps.displayNarration: `reduce` keeps, for each node, only the smallest distance found so far — the breadth-first label.
steps.spoken: Reduce keeps, for each node, only the smallest distance found so far.

steps.title: Differences feed back
steps.displayNarration: New differences feed back for another round, carried on a nested `Product` timestamp so inner iterations stay ordered.
steps.spoken: The new differences feed back for another round, carried on a nested product timestamp so inner iterations stay ordered.

steps.title: Circulate to a fixed point
steps.displayNarration: Differences circulate until they *dissipate* — a fixed point. A `consolidate`/`distinct` step ensures cancelling updates don't loop forever.
steps.spoken: Differences circulate until they dissipate, signalling a fixed point; a consolidation step makes sure cancelling updates do not loop forever.

steps.title: Results leave the scope
steps.displayNarration: When the loop falls quiet, the result `leave`s the iterative scope as final `(node, dist)` pairs.
steps.spoken: When the loop falls quiet, the results leave the scope as final node-distance pairs.

steps.title: Use cases: graph analytics
steps.displayNarration: The same shape powers breadth-first search, strongly connected components, and PageRank — each reacting incrementally to edge changes.
steps.spoken: The same shape powers breadth-first search, strongly connected components, and PageRank, each reacting incrementally to edge changes.

steps.title: End to end
steps.displayNarration: Roots in, around the loop through `join_core`, `reduce`, and `feedback` to a fixed point, and out via `leave` — differential dataflow, end to end.
steps.spoken: Roots in, around the loop through join and reduce and feedback, to a fixed point, and out: differential dataflow, end to end.
